claims.claim_text_normalized: The essential difference between anchor-based and anchor-free detection is how positive and negative training samples are defined.
claims.evidence_quote_short: the essential difference between anchor-based and anchor-free detection is actually how to define positive and negative training samples

claims.claim_text_normalized: When using the same definition of positive and negative samples, there is no obvious performance difference between regressing from a box or a point.
claims.evidence_quote_short: If they adopt the same definition of positive and negative samples during training, there is no obvious difference in the final performance, no matter regressing from a box or a point.

claims.claim_text_normalized: The proposed Adaptive Training Sample Selection (ATSS) automatically selects positive and negative samples based on statistical characteristics of objects.
claims.evidence_quote_short: we propose an Adaptive Training Sample Selection (ATSS) to automatically select positive and negative samples according to statistical characteristics of object.

claims.claim_text_normalized: ATSS significantly improves the performance of both anchor-based and anchor-free detectors.
claims.evidence_quote_short: It significantly improves the performance of anchor-based and anchor-free detectors and bridges the gap between them.

claims.claim_text_normalized: Tiling multiple anchors per location is a useless operation under the proposed ATSS method.
claims.evidence_quote_short: We argue that tiling multiple anchors per location is a useless operation under our proposed method

claims.claim_text_normalized: The proposed ATSS achieves state-of-the-art 50.7% AP on MS COCO without introducing any overhead.
claims.evidence_quote_short: With the newly introduced ATSS, we improve state-of-the-art detectors by a large margin to 50.7% AP without introducing any overhead.

claims.claim_text_normalized: The hyperparameter k in ATSS is robust and the method can be nearly regarded as hyperparameter-free.
claims.evidence_quote_short: the only hyperparameter k is quite robust and the proposed ATSS can be nearly regarded as hyperparameter-free.
